systeme:
Tu rédiges les articles développés d'un journal personnel imprimé, en français, à partir d'un article source complet (souvent en anglais).

Objectif : que le lecteur comprenne le sujet, ses tenants et ses aboutissants, sans lire l'article d'origine.

Règles impératives :
- Fidélité absolue à l'article : n'ajoute AUCUNE information extérieure, ne prête à personne une position qu'il n'a pas exprimée, conserve exactement les chiffres, les noms et les affiliations.
- Longueur : le total des caractères (chapô + intertitres + paragraphes + synthèse) ne doit PAS dépasser la limite indiquée. Vise 90 à 100 % de cette limite, jamais moins de 90 % : la mise en page réserve exactement cette place et un encadré à moitié vide est un défaut. Pour y parvenir, développe les faits, chiffres, acteurs et contexte présents dans l'article (sans rien inventer).
- Format indiqué dans la demande :
  • « long » (demi-page) : 3 à 5 sections, synthèse de 2 phrases ;
  • « court » (quart de page) : 1 ou 2 sections qui donnent les informations clés (faits, chiffres, acteurs, enjeu), puis une synthèse d'une ou deux phrases au maximum.
- Structure :
  • « titre » : titre français informatif, 80 caractères maximum.
  • « chapo » : une phrase qui pose le sujet, 200 caractères maximum.
  • « sections » : selon le format, chacune avec un « intertitre » court et un « texte » d'un paragraphe. Adapte les intertitres au type d'article, par exemple :
      débat ou controverse : Le déclencheur · De quoi parle-t-on · Les arguments pour · Les risques · Les contre-arguments
      annonce ou fait d'actualité : Ce qui est annoncé · Le contexte · Ce que ça change · Les limites
      étude ou recherche : La question · La méthode · Les résultats · Les réserves
      méthode d'entraînement : Le principe · Ce que dit la science · Comment l'appliquer · Les précautions
      réglementation : Ce qui change · Qui est concerné · Le calendrier · Les points de vigilance
  • « synthese » : 2 phrases (format long) ou 1 à 2 phrases (format court) qui résument l'ensemble.
- Style : français soigné, clair, sans tournures calquées sur l'anglais, sans emphase.
- « republication » : si l'article indique qu'il a été publié initialement à une date antérieure (republication), indique « paru initialement en <mois année> » ; sinon chaîne vide.

Réponds uniquement en JSON, selon cette structure :
{"titre": "…", "chapo": "…", "sections": [{"intertitre": "…", "texte": "…"}], "synthese": "…", "republication": ""}
contenu:
Vérification des sources complémentaires : avant de rédiger, vérifie que chaque SOURCE numérotée à partir de 2 traite bien du MÊME fait que la SOURCE 1 (même événement, mêmes acteurs). Ignore entièrement celles qui n'en traitent pas et donne leurs numéros dans « sources_ecartees ». Si, sans elles, la matière ne suffit pas pour un article fiable, réponds seulement {"insuffisant": true, "titre": "…", "texte": "…"} : une brève en français (titre de 90 caractères au plus, 2 à 3 phrases d'environ 450 caractères), uniquement d'après la SOURCE 1.
Format : long
Limite de longueur : 4500 caractères au total.
Édition numérique, lue sur téléphone, sans contrainte de page : la limite suit la matière disponible dans la source. Adapte le nombre de sections à la longueur : 2 sections sous 2 000 caractères, 3 ou 4 jusqu'à 3 500, 4 à 6 au-delà ; même règle de longueur (90 à 100 % de la limite). N'étire jamais une source mince : mieux vaut un article court et exact.
Le texte réunit plusieurs sources sur le même sujet (SOURCE 1, SOURCE 2…). Croise-les sans rien ajouter ; si elles divergent, dis-le en nommant la source.

Titre d'origine : Jensen Huang resigns as Nvidia CEO after espionage scandal wipes out $1.4 trillion in market value

ARTICLE :
SOURCE 1 (The Decoder) :
Jensen Huang resigns as Nvidia CEO after espionage scandal wipes out $1.4 trillion in market value
Jensen Huang resigned as CEO, president, and board member of Nvidia effective immediately, according to a statement on November 12, 2026. The move came after the Wall Street Journal reported that the board was planning to fire Huang following revelations about two extramarital affairs, one of them with a suspected Chinese spy.
Since a New York Times report on October 29 about possible ties to Chinese intelligence, Nvidia has shed roughly $1.4 trillion in market value. CFO Colette Kress is taking over on an interim basis while the board searches for a permanent successor. Harvey C. Jones will serve as the first independent board chair and stressed that business operations continue without disruption.
Replacing Huang will be difficult because Nvidia was built entirely around him. He secured the company's market position through a complex web of alliances with financiers and roughly $300 billion in guarantees for smaller customers. His departure could unravel that structure, which he used to keep major tech rivals at bay and support large parts of the AI industry.
Major customers like Microsoft, Amazon, and Alphabet, along with AI labs like OpenAI and Anthropic, depend heavily on Nvidia's chips, but the company's 75 percent profit margin is pushing them to develop their own, cheaper alternatives. Huang also left no clear succession plan, with more than 60 employees reporting directly to him, leaving both internal and external candidates starting from a weakened position.

SOURCE 2 (Al Jazeera) :
Jensen Huang has resigned as CEO of tech giant Nvidia following his reported affairs with a suspected Chinese spy and a company executive.
The firm’s market value fell below $4 trillion for the first time since July 2025 following Thursday’s announcement, capping a volatile week as Huang’s scandals rocked the company, which supplies most of the chips powering advanced artificial intelligence (AI).
The company appointed Nvidia Chief Financial Officer and Executive Vice President Colette Kress as interim CEO on Thursday and named its first-ever board chair, Harvey C Jones, who has been a venture investor for the last three decades.
Nvidia’s board met on Wednesday night to discuss ousting Huang, whose relationship with an alleged Chinese spy triggered investigations by the FBI, the United States Congress and the California-based chip maker. Nvidia is also facing a shareholder class-action lawsuit.
The alleged Chinese intelligence asset, Alice Huang, is a former executive at Singapore-based Megaspeed, Nvidia’s primary business partner in Southeast Asia. Founded in 2023, Megaspeed has been investigated over whether it helped Chinese companies access its $4.8bn stock of powerful Nvidia chips.
The affair has raised national security concerns in the US, which restricts chip sales to China over concerns that the Chinese military, intelligence agencies or companies could use the advanced technology.
Huang, 63, is Nvidia’s longtime cofounder, president and CEO. A close ally of US President Donald Trump, he has pushed to ease US restrictions on chip exports to China. Trump said earlier this week that Huang told him he had “absolutely no idea” that he was in a relationship with an intelligence operative.
Congressional investigations
Huang has agreed to testify before Congress, House of Representatives’ Foreign Affairs Committee Chairman Brian Mast told reporters on Thursday. Senate and House Democrats are also launching a probe into the Trump administration’s plans to approve AI chip sales to Chinese companies.
Huang cofounded the Silicon Valley company in 1993 and owns about 3.6 percent of Nvidia’s stock, making him one of the richest people in the world. He is a powerful figure in the AI industry, which has driven record stock market and wider economic gains. The company is set to report quarterly earnings on Tuesday.
Aleksandar Tomic, associate dean for strategy, innovation, and technology at Boston College, told Al Jazeera that the “resignation of Jensen Huang will have an outsized effect compared to a similar event at another large corporation given the relatively flat structure of Nvidia”.
But he said that Nvidia, an AI bellwether, “is in a very strong position” that will enable the company to transition from Huang’s leadership. Tomic called Huang’s resignation a “speed bump” for the company.
“Nvidia is a strong company with a strong product, and this is a sudden event, not a product of corporate struggle,” he said. “It may take some time to figure out the succession process, but Nvidia can handle it as they approach it from the position of strength.”
Nvidia’s board, which hired a law firm to investigate the affair with Alice Huang, met to decide Huang’s fate on Wednesday shortly after The New York Times reported that Huang also had an extramarital relationship with an Nvidia vice president who reports to him.
On Thursday, the Reuters news agency reported, citing two people familiar with the matter, that Huang also had an intimate relationship with a second company employee.
Nvidia’s stock has tumbled since the scandal erupted, leaving it trading at its lowest multiple of expected earnings in 14 years, Reuters reported.

SOURCE 3 (The Times of India) :
Nvidia shares plunged as much as 14 per cent during Thursday's Wall Street trading session after the shock resignation of chief executive Jensen Huang, extending a weeks-long selloff in the chipmaker amid concerns over the company's leadership and the future of the artificial intelligence boom. The stock recovered some of its losses during the session, eventually closing 4.3 per cent lower at $166.19.
The latest decline has dealt another blow to Nvidia's market valuation, with the company shedding nearly $500 billion in market value since the close of trading last week. Its shares are now around 30 per cent below the record high touched on October 6, wiping out more than $1 trillion in market capitalisation over the past month. Nvidia's market value slipped below $4 trillion, a level it had not breached since July 2025, reported Reuters. Huang has lost his spot in world's top 10 richest people.
The selloff marks a sharp reversal for a company that became the world's most valuable publicly listed business on the back of the global AI boom. Nvidia's graphics processing units (GPUs), which power artificial intelligence systems and data centres, made it a central player in the technology industry and one of Wall Street's biggest market drivers. 
Its shares had surged more than 1,700% over four years before the recent correction, while its market capitalisation had briefly crossed $5 trillion.
Huang's departure has also taken a toll on his personal fortune. The Nvidia co-founder, who had been among the world's 10 richest people, has seen his wealth fall sharply alongside the company's stock. According to Forbes' Real-Time Billionaires rankings, he slipped two places from eighth to tenth earlier this week. His estimated fortune subsequently fell further, pushing him out of the top 10 to 13th position.

The fallout extended beyond Nvidia to companies closely linked to its AI ecosystem. Nvidia-backed cloud computing firm CoreWeave fell 8.1 per cent, while Nebius plunged 18 per cent after cutting its 2026 revenue forecast amid delays in adding third-party capacity. Super Micro Computer also dropped 12%. However, rival chipmakers Advanced Micro Devices and Broadcom gained more than 4 per cent each, as investors assessed whether Nvidia's leadership turmoil could create opportunities for competitors.
 Nvidia is also due to report its quarterly results next week, with investors watching its revenue growth and outlook.
The turbulence in Nvidia also played out against a volatile session on Wall Street, although the broader market managed to recover most of its early losses. The S&P 500 fell 0.4% to 7,592.40, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average declined 189.40 points, or 0.4%, to 52,297.09. The Nasdaq Composite also shed 0.4% to close at 25,366.09, after falling as much as 1.6% earlier in the session. Rising oil prices following US President Donald Trump's remarks on Iran added to market pressure, with Brent crude climbing 3.3% to $95.82 a barrel.
